newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan stocks close lower in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan stocks close lower in cautious trade.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Tuesday 0.06 percent lower with shares from only 20 companies being traded out of the 48 listed, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 647.75 points from 648.14 on Monday.

ONA group, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, closed unchanged at 815 dirhams. The second largest private group, SNI, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, edged down four dirhams to 746 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Wafabank remained unchanged at 825 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur also closed unchanged at 580 dirhams with 4,448 shares changing hands.
First tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January 1996, jumped 20 dirhams to 1,400 dirhams.

In the energy sector, Samir dipped three dirhams to 342 dirhams. Mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter rose one dirham to 560 dirhams. Total traded volume on the official market was 26 million dirhams from 23 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 40 million million dirhams from 64 million dirhams with main trade in cement firm Lafarge Ciments, a broker at Sogebourse said.
